The Figure 1 caption describes the patient as intubated on PRVC ventilation combined with iNO therapy, but the text has iNO discontinued on day 8 and PRVC mode begun on day 13.
The text states blood cultures remained negative throughout the clinical course, while a later passage mentions bloodstream infection; a central line culture grew Enterobacter hormaechei on day 27.
The text says the following day FiO_(2) remained at approximately 0.70, while Table 2 gives FiO_(2) 1.0 at DOL 2; the text day is not labelled as a DOL.

Figures 3 to 8 are reprinted from the authors' previous publication as representative images, although the text says they illustrate features observed in the present patient; their attribution to this patient is not established.
The pathogenesis of PPHN is described as multifactorial and the hyperthermic episodes as compatible with dysautonomia; these are hedged author interpretations.
Table 2 cell for sPAP on DOL 1 reads "Not quantified"; recorded as not performed.

claims.text: A male neonate was delivered by cesarean section at an estimated 38 weeks after prenatal ultrasound showed long-bone shortening and bowing, thoracic hypoplasia and contractures, with fetal growth restriction. Apgar scores were 3, 3, 6 and 9, birth weight was 3440 g, and examination showed dysmorphic features, a hypoplastic chest and abnormal finger and toe positioning. He received non-invasive ventilation, was transferred to the NICU and was intubated at 5 h of life for worsening respiratory distress.

claims.text: Serial echocardiograms confirmed severe suprasystemic PPHN with right-to-left shunting and right ventricular pressure overload, and the oxygenation index reached 48 on day 3. Support was escalated with HFOV, iNO 25 ppm and catecholamines; ECMO criteria were met but extracorporeal support was not initiated because of instability. Workup found a structurally normal heart and negative blood cultures, and whole-exome sequencing identified two pathogenic LIFR nonsense variants in trans, establishing Stüve–Wiedemann syndrome.
